capitals.name: Maynila (Manila, Intramuros)
capitals.note: 'situated along the modern-day district of Intramuros in the city of Manila, at the southern bank of the Pasig River'; burned in May 1570, partly rebuilt by 1571, replaced by the Spanish walled city.

rulers.name: Salalila
rulers.note: Infobox 'c. 1500s-c. 1521'; the page gives no reign dates.

rulers.name: Ache (Rajah Matanda)
rulers.note: Infobox 'c. 1521 - August 1572'; the Maynila state ends in June 1571 but Matanda lived on to August 1572 (Rajah Matanda page), with his nephew Rajah Sulayman sharing paramount rule by 1570.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the years before Cliopatria's row: 'Manila was probably founded as a Bornean trading colony about 1500' (infobox: 'Establishment of Maynila and conversion to Islam: c. 1500'; the page also gives oral traditions of the 1250s and calls that date doubtful). The page gives no area; a single bayan on the Pasig's south bank. Cliopatria's Brunei shapes carry Manila until 1520, which the Brunei dossier already removes ('political influence ... not considered to have extended to military or political rule').

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1521 shape (2,955 km2, 8 cells) cut to its one Philippine cell at the Pasig mouth: the other six cells lie in Okinawa, in the Ryukyu Islands

keyframe_review.note: The shape's centroid (126.85 E, 24.97 N) is in the Ryukyu Islands; only one of the eight cells is Manila (14.58 N, 121.01 E). The page places Maynila 'at the southern bank of the Pasig River' and nowhere mentions the Ryukyu. The Tondo dossier's contest zone (a 20 km disc at the Pasig mouth) shares this cell. No infobox area to compare.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1526 shape (3,359 km2, 9 cells) cut to its one Philippine cell at the Pasig mouth; the other eight lie in the Ryukyu Islands (Okinawa and Ishigaki)

keyframe_review.note: Same fault as 1521: the extra Ryukyu cell added in 1526 (24.4 N, 123.9 E, Ishigaki) is not Maynila's. The Maynila page records no territorial change between 1521 and 1570.

correction.text: Maynila has no shape after 24 June 1571: the page says the Spanish declaration 'effectively end[ed] Maynila's history as an independent polity'. The Cliopatria cells for 1572-1594 are 11 cells in the Ryukyu Islands (Okinawa), none in the Philippines; Manila passes to the Spanish Empire

keyframe_review.note: 4,392 km2, centroid 127.8 E, 26.7 N: Okinawa, not Manila. Ache died in August 1572 (infobox) but as a Spanish ally; Rajah Sulayman was proclaimed paramount ruler on his death (Rajah Matanda page), a title inside Spanish Manila.

correction.text: No Maynila after 1571; the shape is the same Okinawa outline as 1572. Manila is the Spanish city (spanish-empire)

keyframe_review.note: Same fault as 1572, years 1595-1599: the shape is Japanese territory (Ryukyu) and Maynila ended in 1571.

ledger.note: c. 1500: Maynila is founded on the south bank of the Pasig. 'Manila was probably founded as a Bornean trading colony about 1500' (infobox: 'Establishment of Maynila and conversion to Islam: c. 1500'). Brunei's 'political influence over Maynila is not considered to have extended to military or political rule'.

region.text: the Pasig river mouth between Tondo and Maynila

ledger.note: c. 1520: Tondo presses on Maynila's territory. Ache's cousin, ruler of Tondo, was 'slyly' taking over 'territory belonging to Maynila' while Ache's mother ruled; infobox 'Death of Rajah Salalila and territorial conflicts with Tondo: c. before 1521'. Year bridged from 'before 1521'; where the border ran is not stated.
c. 1521: the conflict is over by the time Ache rules (c. 1521-1572); the page gives no treaty or last battle, so the year is a bridge.

ledger.note: May 1570: Martin de Goiti attacks Maynila. 'This was the political situation encountered by Martin de Goiti when he attacked Maynila in May of that year'; the 'Battle of Maynila' 'ended with a fire that destroyed the fortified settlement of Maynila' (infobox: 'Battle of Manila: 1570').

region.text: Maynila, the fortified bayan on the south bank of the Pasig (today Intramuros) and its hinterland, drawn as a 12 km disc by the researcher

ledger.note: June 1571: the fighting ends. The Battle of Bangkusay (3 June 1571) was 'the last local resistance to Spanish occupation of the Pasig delta'; 'Tarik Sulayman, supported by Rajah Sulayman' was defeated off Tondo. Legazpi had allied with Lakandula and the rulers of Maynila and Tondo 'made a deal' that let him claim Maynila for Spain (Rajah Matanda page).

wars.name: Spanish conquest of Maynila (Battle of Maynila)

zones.text: Maynila, the fortified bayan on the south bank of the Pasig (today Intramuros) and its hinterland, drawn as a 12 km disc by the researcher

wars.outcome: Goiti's May 1570 attack burned the settlement; in 1571 Legazpi allied with Lakandula of Tondo, the rulers of Maynila made a deal that let Spain claim the city, Bangkusay (3 June 1571) ended local resistance, and Manila was declared a Spanish city on 24 June 1571.
wars.note: Bangkusay: 'On June 3, 1571, Tarik Sulayman, supported by Rajah Sulayman, led his troops down the Pampanga River'; the Spanish victory is in the Battle of Bangkusay Channel page, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Bangkusay_Channel. The Limahong attack of 1574 and the Tondo Conspiracy of 1587-1588 are outside the state's life and are not on the pages opened.

wars.name: Maynila-Tondo territorial conflict
wars.outcome: No result recorded; the dispute predates Ache's rule (c. 1521).
wars.note: The page gives the dispute in a fragment and an infobox line ('c. before 1521'), with no year, treaty or border.

certainty.note: A single walled bayan on the Pasig; no frontier is recorded, and Maynila's hinterland and the Tondo border are not given. The Spanish city of 1571 is the only sharp line.

notes: Cliopatria 'Maynila' (4 shapes, 1521..1599) is mislabelled: each shape is eight to eleven cells, of which only one (14.58 N, 121.01 E, the Pasig mouth) is Manila and the rest lie in the Ryukyu Islands (1521: 6, 1526: 8, 1572 and 1595: 10-11 cells of Okinawa, none in the Philippines; centroid 127.8 E, 26.7 N). The pages opened never mention the Ryukyu. Verdicts: 1521 and 1526 adjusted to the Philippine cell; 1572 and 1595 wrong (no Maynila after 24 June 1571). Start: the page says c. 1500 ('probably founded as a Bornean trading colony about 1500'; a doubtful 1258 tradition), so a keyframe 1500-1520 is new; Cliopatria starts 1521. The Brunei dossier already removes Manila from its shapes (influence, not rule). Tondo's dossier (se-02-d) mirrors the c. 1520-1521 contest and the 1570-1571 Spanish contest with the same 20 km and 40 km Manila discs. The Maynila page's fragments for the Tondo conflict give no border; the 12 km core disc is the researcher's drawing (one grid cell) and the Maynila-Tondo split inside the Pasig delta is not known. Not on the pages: the 1574 Limahong attack and the Tondo Conspiracy of 1587-1588 (outside the state's life). The state is drawn to June 1571 (Spanish declaration), though Ache lived to August 1572. Counterparts needing dossiers: none; spanish-empire and tondo exist. The fetch tool returns a model summary of each page; quotation marks mean 'as the fetched text gave it'.
